annotation_description: The player has 2 untapped lands and several castable spells but chose to do nothing. Gran-Gran costs {U} and could be cast, providing a body on board and its looting ability when tapped. Artist's Talent costs {1}{R} and could also be cast to enable card filtering. Boomerang Basics could bounce the opponent's Otter token. Firebending Lesson could kill the opponent's 1/1 Otter token. Passing the turn with 2 mana available and multiple playable options wastes tempo in an early game where board development matters. At minimum, Gran-Gran should have been cast as a 1/2 body that generates card selection and enables future cost reduction with Lessons in graveyard.

Playing Riverpyre Verge now means Spirebluff Canal will likely be the 4th land played (entering tapped), losing tempo on a critical turn. Spirebluff Canal enters untapped only with 2 or fewer other lands, so it should be played earlier.

Duelist of the Mind has flying and vigilance, meaning it can attack for 1 damage through the air with zero downside (stays untapped to block). The opponent has no flyers to block it. This is free damage left on the table.

Casting Duelist of the Mind in the precombat main phase is suboptimal. The existing Duelist of the Mind on the battlefield has power equal to cards drawn this turn, and casting spells/creatures before combat doesn't increase its power. More importantly, Frostcliff Siege (choosing Jeskai) would be a stronger play here - it provides card advantage whenever creatures deal combat damage. With a Duelist of the Mind already on board (flying, vigilance), casting Frostcliff Siege before combat would let the Duelist attack and draw a card immediately this turn. The second Duelist of the Mind entering as a 0/3 (having drawn 0 cards this turn) doesn't contribute to combat this turn. Additionally, casting the creature before combat when holding Boomerang Basics (a trick/noncreature spell) means missing the opportunity to sequence optimally - playing Frostcliff Siege would also trigger Artist's Talent-style synergies with the Stormchaser's Talent otter's prowess.

Discarded Quantum Riddler instead of Frostcliff Siege, despite reasoning that concluded Frostcliff Siege should be discarded. Quantum Riddler has Warp {1}{U} making it castable cheaply as a 2/2, but Frostcliff Siege (Jeskai mode) provides a consistent card draw engine that synergizes extremely well with two flying Duelist of the Mind on board - each combat damage trigger draws a card, which directly pumps Duelist power. However, the Riddler's Warp ability and late-game potential also have value, making this a close call.

With 3 mana available (UUG from Steam Vents + 2x Willowrush Verge), casting Stormchaser's Talent for U is fine value, but the sequencing and choice could be debated. The opponent has two Duelist of the Mind on board which are threatening. Boomerang Basics (U) could bounce one of the Duelists, which is a tempo play that also draws a card since it's the opponent's permanent being returned (no, it only draws if you controlled it). Gran-Gran (U) is a 1/2 that loots when tapped AND reduces noncreature spell costs with 3+ Lessons in graveyard - important synergy with the Lesson-heavy hand. However, casting Stormchaser's Talent to get a 1/1 prowess blocker is reasonable given the two Duelists threatening in the air. The main concern is whether Artist's Talent (1R) could have been cast - with UUG available, there's no R source unless Steam Vents taps for R. Steam Vents can tap for U or R, so the player could cast Artist's Talent (1R = using Steam Vents for R + Willowrush for U). Artist's Talent provides looting on noncreature spells which is strong with this hand full of noncreature spells. But Stormchaser's Talent gives a body to block the Duelists and leaves mana open for Firebending Lesson to kill a Duelist. Actually, casting Stormchaser's Talent for U leaves UG open - not enough for Firebending Lesson (R). So this sequencing doesn't enable holding up removal. The play is defensible but there were arguments for other lines.

Willowrush Verge has an unconditional '{T}: Add {U}' ability. The player incorrectly believed they only had G available, missing that they could cast either Boomerang Basics or Stormchaser's Talent. Bouncing an opponent's Duelist of the Mind with Boomerang Basics while the opponent is completely tapped out would have been a strong tempo play, removing a key threat.

Passed without casting Frostcliff Siege before combat. Either Temur mode (giving the summoning-sick Duelist haste to attack, plus +1/+0 and trample to both Duelists) or Jeskai mode (drawing cards on combat damage) would have been significantly better cast precombat rather than held. Passing loses the benefit of the enchantment for this turn's combat.

Declined to cast Boomerang Basics with 2 untapped lands available. Bouncing opponent's Stormchaser's Talent (their key enchantment engine) would have been a strong tempo play, forcing them to spend mana replaying it. Alternatively, bouncing the Otter Token removes their only blocker for next turn's attacks.

Casting a second Stormchaser's Talent when already having one on the battlefield is low value - the legendary rule doesn't apply to Classes, but the first level ability just creates another 1/1 Otter. Meanwhile, Sonnet Stoic is at 11 life facing two Duelist of the Mind (which can be very large with card draw), and has Boomerang Basics available to bounce one of those Duelists. Additionally, Artist's Talent at 1R would provide a much stronger value engine (loot on noncreature spells, and can level up for cost reduction). The sequencing is also questionable - they should consider bouncing a Duelist first to stabilize, or casting Artist's Talent for ongoing value rather than getting a second 1/1 token that won't meaningfully help against the opponent's flyers.

At 11 life facing two Duelist of the Mind with flying, bouncing the opponent's Stormchaser's Talent instead of a Duelist removes a value engine but doesn't address the immediate flying damage clock. Stormchaser's Talent only costs U to replay, while bouncing a Duelist (costs 1U to replay) would directly reduce incoming damage and buy more time.

DSV3 Libby passed their precombat main with 4 untapped lands and strong plays available. Fear of Missing Out (1R) would ETB loot (increasing Duelist of the Mind's power via the draw), create a 2/3 attacker, and with delirium active (5+ card types in graveyard), grant extra combat phases. Stormchaser's Talent could also create another token. The opponent is at 11 life with all lands tapped and only two small Otter tokens as defense.

Combustion Technique would deal 4 damage (2 base + 2 Lessons in graveyard: Boomerang Basics x2) to Duelist of the Mind (0-power/3 toughness with flying and vigilance), cleanly killing and exiling it. Removing this flying vigilance threat would free up the Otters to attack more effectively and prevent future Duelist value. Artist's Talent builds long-term value but doesn't address the board threat.

Attacking both 1/1 Otter tokens into a Duelist of the Mind (1/3 with vigilance) means one Otter will trade for just 1 point of chip damage getting through. At 11 life vs opponent's 20 life, trading a prowess creature for 1 damage is a poor rate. The Otters have prowess and could become meaningful threats when casting spells later.

DSV3 Libby passed priority precombat with Duelist of the Mind on board (currently 0/3 power). Casting spells that draw cards precombat would pump Duelist's power for the attack. Fear of Missing Out (1R) would trigger a draw, and with 5 card types in graveyard enabling delirium, would grant an extra combat phase with untap. Boomerang Basics targeting an opponent's permanent would trigger Duelist's crime ability for another draw. Combined, Duelist could attack as a 2/3 or 3/3 across multiple combats against a tapped-out opponent at 11 life.

Casting Duelist of the Mind (a creature) before combat instead of casting noncreature spells first to pump the existing Duelist of the Mind's power. Boomerang Basics targeting an opponent's Stormchaser's Talent or Otter Token would trigger the crime ability on the existing Duelist (draw + discard), increasing its power for combat. With opponent completely tapped out, there's no reason to hold back.

Only attacked with one Duelist of the Mind when both Duelists have flying and vigilance. Both could attack for free since vigilance means they stay untapped for blocking, and flying means the opponent's tapped Otter Tokens couldn't block anyway. This wastes damage against an opponent at 11 life.

Bounced Gran-Gran (a cheap 1-mana creature that can easily be replayed) instead of Artist's Talent, which is a much higher-value enchantment that likely has level-up investment. Artist's Talent at higher levels provides cost reduction and +2 noncombat damage, making it the most impactful permanent to bounce for tempo. Alternatively, a leveled-up Stormchaser's Talent would also be a better target.

With delirium already active (creature, land, sorcery, enchantment, instant in graveyard), Fear of Missing Out would enable extra combat phases on future turns alongside two Duelists of the Mind, which could be devastating. The 2/3 body is also more impactful than a 1/1 Otter token.

With Sonnet Stoic at 8 life and two Duelist of the Mind ready to attack, bouncing Toph (a 3/4 blocker that costs 4 mana to replay) would have been more impactful than bouncing Artist's Talent (a value enchantment). Removing the biggest blocker enables more combat damage to push toward lethal, and the tempo loss of replaying a 4-mana creature is much larger than replaying a 2-mana enchantment.

Toph (3/4) was held back from attacking despite being unable to block the opponent's primary threats (two Duelist of the Mind with flying). Toph attacking would either deal 3 damage or force a favorable trade with a 0/3 Duelist. Keeping Toph back provides no defensive value against flying creatures.

At 8 life facing two flying Duelist of the Mind with vigilance, the priority should be removing a Duelist rather than deploying a 1/2 ground creature. Combustion Technique would deal 4 damage (2 base + 2 Lessons in graveyard) to kill a Duelist, significantly reducing the flying clock. Gran-Gran doesn't block flyers and doesn't address the immediate survival concern.

At 8 life facing two flying Duelist of the Mind with vigilance, Sonnet Stoic chose to cast Artist's Talent for long-term value instead of using Combustion Technique to kill one of the Duelists. Combustion Technique would deal 4 damage (2 base + 2 Lessons in graveyard), enough to kill a 3-toughness Duelist. With flying threats putting significant pressure at low life, removing a threat is much more important than building incremental value.

Duelist of the Mind has vigilance, so it doesn't tap when attacking and is already untapped. Targeting it with Fear of Missing Out's untap trigger accomplishes nothing. Fear of Missing Out itself is tapped from attacking and could be untapped to attack again in the additional combat phase for 2 extra damage against an opponent at 8 life.

Gran-Gran is a valuable creature (card filtering + potential cost reduction with Lessons), and the earthbent Willowrush Verge would return to the battlefield tapped when it dies due to earthbend's ability. Blocking with Willowrush Verge instead of Gran-Gran would save the same amount of life while preserving the more valuable permanent.

Chump-blocked Toph with a Duelist of the Mind (0/3) to prevent just 3 damage while at 15 life against an opponent at 4 life. The Duelist is a key win condition that could have significant power on the next attack turn with card draws.

At 4 life facing a Duelist of the Mind that has been dealing 3+ damage per turn, Sonnet Stoic passed with 2 open mana and Boomerang Basics in hand. Bouncing Duelist of the Mind would remove the primary threat and buy a critical turn. The Duelist could easily deal lethal next turn with draws boosting its power.

At 2 life facing Duelist of the Mind which threatens lethal next turn, Sonnet Stoic passed without casting any spells despite having Boomerang Basics (U) available with Breeding Pool untapped to bounce the Duelist. They also potentially had Combustion Technique available depending on Artist's Talent level. Passing here likely means dying next turn.

Opponent is at 2 life. Duelist of the Mind's power equals cards drawn this turn (currently 1 from draw step). Casting Winternight Stories would draw 3 cards, making Duelist's power 4, enabling a lethal attack. Instead, the player appears focused on leveling Stormchaser's Talent which doesn't draw cards and doesn't enable lethal this turn.
